about: POST /token, /introspection, /revoke, /tokenexchange, /deviceauthorization, /register; GET and POST /userinfo; GET /claimdescription. Recorded against the api as it was before the family switched to the model (docs/v0.9.5/data-model.md). Every target is as.invalid, which RFC 6761 guarantees never resolves, so a well-formed request ends in the same 500 on any machine. Every credential here is a dummy. GET /claimdescription is the one case that leaves the machine: it fetches IANA's registry, so its text is volatile and only its status (and that the body is not JSON) is held.

cases.name: token: an empty body
cases.changed: The model requires token_endpoint, the one member no handler can do without. Until then the api made the outbound call with no URL and answered axios's "Invalid URL" as a 500, which read as the far end failing.

body.error: The outbound call failed: Invalid URL
Refusing the request: `token_endpoint` is required. GET /api-docs describes what oauthToken takes.

cases.name: token: a body that is an array
cases.changed: The body must be a JSON object. Until then an array reached convertToOAuth2Format() and the call failed with "Invalid URL" (500).

body.error: The outbound call failed: Invalid URL
Refusing the request: `token_endpoint` must be a JSON object. GET /api-docs describes what oauthToken takes.
